title: Programming Next Steps: Functions, Lists and AI

pages.c24-p01: Describe the data types int, double, float, string, char and bool, and choose the most suitable data type for a value
pages.c24-p02: Explain why programmers use methods (functions) to avoid repetition and decompose problems, and write and call a static void method
pages.c24-p03: Use parameters and arguments to pass values into a method, so one method can work with different data
pages.c24-p04: Write methods that return a value, and explain the difference between a void method and a method with a return type
pages.c24-p05: Explain the scope of a variable, and the difference between local and global (class-level) variables
pages.c24-p06: Declare an array, access its elements using an index that starts at 0, and loop through it with a for loop
pages.c24-p07: Use a List to store a collection that can grow and shrink, using Add, Remove, Count and foreach, and choose between a list and an array
pages.c24-p08: Use loops to process a list: find the total, average and largest value, search for an item and count matches
pages.c24-p09: Evaluate the benefits and limitations of using generative AI to help write code, and review and verify the code it produces
pages.c24-p10: Plan, develop, test and refine a program in stages, using methods, a list and a test table

q.q: Which C# data type stores whole numbers such as 42 or -7?
q.why: int stores integers, which are whole numbers with no decimal part.

q.q: Which C# data type can only hold the values true or false?
q.why: bool is the Boolean type: it only has two possible values.

q.q: Both values are ints. What is displayed by Console.WriteLine(10 / 4);?
q.why: Dividing two integers gives an integer, so the .5 is thrown away.

q.q: Which line correctly declares a char variable?
q.why: A char uses single quotes; a string would need double quotes.

q.q: A program stores a postcode such as BT74 6AA. Which data type should it use?
q.why: A postcode contains letters, digits and a space, and no maths is done with it, so it is text.

q.q: What is displayed? int mark = 45; bool passed = mark >= 50; Console.WriteLine(passed);
q.why: 45 >= 50 is false, and C# displays a Boolean with a capital letter.

q.q: Why does the line float speed = 12.5; cause an error?
o: A float cannot store decimal values
12.5 is a double unless it ends with f
The word float needs a capital F
A float can only hold whole numbers
q.why: Decimal literals are doubles in C#; write 12.5f to make a float.

q.q: What is the result of (double)7 / 2 in C#?
q.why: Casting 7 to a double first means the division keeps its decimal part.

q.q: In general (non-C#) terms, a number with a decimal point is called a…
q.why: Float or real is the general name; C# uses double or float.

q.q: A pupil stores the number of lengths swum as a double. Why is int a better choice?
o: An int can also store text if needed
Lengths swum are always whole numbers
A double cannot store numbers over 100
An int is shown with a decimal point
q.why: Whole-number counts should use int; it is the type that fits the data.

q.q: What is a method?
o: A variable that stores a list of values
A loop that repeats code forever
A named block of code that does one task
An error message from the compiler
q.why: A method groups instructions under a name so they can be called.

q.q: What does the DRY rule stand for?
q.why: Methods help you avoid repeating the same code.

q.q: In our C# programs, where should a new method be written?
o: Inside the curly brackets of Main
Inside class Program but outside Main
q.why: Methods sit inside the class, alongside Main, not inside it.

q.q: Which of these is a correct method header?
q.why: A header has no semicolon and the order is static, return type, name, brackets.

q.q: Which name follows the usual C# style for a method?
q.why: Methods use PascalCase; camelCase like totalPrice is used for variables.

q.q: Breaking a big problem down into smaller parts that are easier to solve is called…
q.why: Decomposition breaks problems down; abstraction removes unnecessary detail.

q.q: Main calls ShowLine(); twice, and ShowLine displays one row of dashes. How many rows of dashes appear?
q.why: The method runs once for every call, so it runs twice.

q.q: What happens when a program reaches the line ShowBanner(); in Main?
o: It runs the rest of Main first, then ShowBanner
It copies ShowBanner into Main permanently
It runs ShowBanner once and then ends
It runs ShowBanner, then carries on in Main
q.why: A call jumps to the method, runs it, then returns to the line after the call.

q.q: A banner appears in 6 places in a program. If it is put in a method and the quiz is renamed, how many places need changing?
q.why: The banner is written once inside the method, so only that place changes.

q.q: Ciara writes ShowMenu() while Tom writes PrintReceipt() for the same program. Which benefit of methods does this show?
o: The program needs fewer data types
The program uses much less memory
Loops are no longer needed at all
Different people can write different parts
q.why: Decomposing into methods lets a team share out the work.

q.q: What is a parameter?
o: The actual value passed in when calling a method
The value sent back from a method by return
A variable in a method header that receives a value
The name given to a method in its header
q.why: Parameters are declared in the header and receive the arguments.

q.q: In the call Greet("Sam", 14); what are "Sam" and 14?
q.why: Values passed in a method call are arguments.

q.q: Which memory trick matches the terms on this topic?
q.why: Parameter = placeholder; argument = actual value.

q.q: The header is static void Order(string item, int qty). Which call is valid?
q.why: It needs a string then an int, in that order.

q.q: What is displayed? static void Show(int x) { Console.WriteLine(x * 2); } is called with Show(6);
q.why: 6 is copied into x, and 6 times 2 is 12.

q.q: Why does Order("Chips", "2"); fail for the header static void Order(string item, int qty)?
o: "2" is a string but qty must be an int
There are too many arguments in it
Strings cannot be passed to methods
q.why: Each argument must match its parameter's data type.

q.q: int age = 13; Greet(age); The header is static void Greet(int years). What value does years hold?
q.why: The value of the argument is copied in; the names do not need to match.

q.q: Repeat("Go", 2); runs a loop for (int i = 0; i < times; i++) that writes word and a space. What appears?
q.why: i takes the values 0 and 1, so the loop runs twice.

q.q: How many arguments must a call to PrintReceipt(string item, int quantity, double price) have?
q.why: One argument is needed for each of the three parameters.

q.q: Why use one ShowRound(string title) method instead of a separate method for each round?
o: One method can work with different data
Separate methods are not allowed in C#
Parameters stop a method being changed
q.why: Parameters let the same code run with different values.

q.q: Which keyword sends a value back from a method?
q.why: return sends a value back and ends the method.

q.q: What is the return type of static double Average(int a, int b)?
q.why: The type written just before the method name is the return type.

q.q: Square returns n * n. What is stored in x by int x = Square(4);?
q.why: 4 times 4 is 16, which replaces the call.

q.q: Which of these methods does not return a value?
q.why: void means nothing is returned.

q.q: Add returns a + b. What is displayed by Console.WriteLine(Add(2, 3) * 2);?
q.why: Add(2, 3) returns 5, and 5 times 2 is 10.

q.q: static bool IsAdult(int age) { return age >= 18; } What does IsAdult(18) return?
q.why: 18 >= 18 is true, because >= includes equal to.

q.q: The error "not all code paths return a value" means…
o: the method has too many parameters
a method with a return type can end without return
the method was never called from Main
a void method has been given a name
q.why: A method with a return type must reach a return on every route through it.

q.q: In GCSE terms, what is a procedure?
o: A subroutine that does not return a value
A subroutine that returns a value
A variable declared inside a method
A loop written inside a method
q.why: Procedures do a job; functions return a value.

q.q: static double Average(int a, int b) { return (a + b) / 2; } What does Average(3, 4) return?
q.why: (a + b) / 2 is integer division, so 7 / 2 gives 3 before it is turned into a double.

q.q: ToFahrenheit returns c * 9 / 5 + 32. What does ToFahrenheit(10) return?
q.why: 10 times 9 is 90, divided by 5 is 18, plus 32 is 50.

q.q: What is the scope of a variable?
o: The data type that the variable holds
The value currently stored in it
The part of a program where it can be used
The number of times it can change
q.why: Scope is where a variable exists and can be used.

q.q: Where is a local variable declared?
o: Inside the class, outside every method
In the namespace, outside the class
q.why: Local variables belong to the method or block they are declared in.

q.q: In C#, what is the nearest thing to a global variable?
o: A variable declared at the top of Main
A variable declared inside a for loop
A parameter in the header of Main
A static variable in the class, outside every method
q.why: Class-level static variables can be used by every method in the class.

q.q: Error CS0103 says a name "does not exist in the current context". What does this usually mean?
o: A variable is used outside its scope
A variable has the wrong data type
A semicolon is missing at the end
q.why: The variable is not visible where it is being used.

q.q: Are a method's parameters local or global?
o: Local: they only exist inside their method
Global: every method can use them
Local, but only if they are strings
Global, but only when called from Main
q.why: Parameters belong to their own method.

q.q: Two different methods each declare a local variable called total. What happens?
o: A compile error, as names must be unique
The second total overwrites the first
Both methods share the same value
Nothing goes wrong: they are separate
q.why: Each local variable lives in its own scope, so the names do not clash.

q.q: Which is the best reason to prefer local variables to global ones?
o: They are quicker to type than globals
Other methods cannot change them by accident
They can store any type of data
They last for the whole program
q.why: Limiting where a value can be changed makes bugs easier to find.

q.q: static int score = 0; is declared in the class. Main calls AddPoints(4); then AddPoints(6); and each call adds its parameter to score. What is score now?
q.why: Both calls change the same class-level variable: 0 + 4 + 6 = 10.

q.q: A pupil declares int count = 0; inside a foreach loop and adds 1 for each match. What is the main problem?
o: count resets each pass and is gone after the loop
count cannot be an int inside a loop
foreach loops cannot contain IF statements
count must be declared as a string instead
q.why: Declare count before the loop so it keeps its value and stays in scope.

q.q: After for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { } a pupil needs the value of i. What is the best fix?
o: Change i into a string variable
Declare i before the loop starts
Put the word static inside the loop
q.why: A variable declared before the loop is still in scope after it.

q.q: In C#, what is the index of the first element in an array?
q.why: C# arrays are zero-indexed.

q.q: Which statement best describes an array?
o: A fixed number of values of the same type
Any number of values of any data type
One value that can change its data type
A growing collection of mixed data types
q.why: Arrays have a fixed size and one data type.
Index 0 is 5, index 1 is 8, index 2 is 2.

q.q: int[] a = { 5, 8, 2, 9 }; What is a.Length?
q.why: There are four elements, even though the last index is 3.

q.q: An array has a Length of 10. What is the index of its last element?
q.why: The last index is always Length - 1.

q.q: Which line creates an array with space for 6 integers?
q.why: Use the type with [] on the left and new int[6] on the right.

q.q: int[] s = new int[3]; s[0] = 4; What does Console.WriteLine(s[1]); display?
q.why: Elements of a new int array start at the default value 0.

q.q: A loop uses for (int i = 0; i <= arr.Length; i++) to display arr[i]. What happens?
o: It crashes when it reaches arr[arr.Length]
It misses out the first element
It runs forever and never stops
q.why: There is no element at index Length, so an IndexOutOfRangeException occurs.

q.q: A loop uses for (int i = 1; i < arr.Length; i++) to display arr[i]. What is wrong?
o: It never displays the first element
It crashes at the end of the array
It runs one time too many
q.why: Starting at 1 skips index 0; this off-by-one error gives no crash, so it is easy to miss.

q.q: int[] goals = { 2, 0, 3, 1 }; What is goals[0] + goals[3]?
q.why: goals[0] is 2 and goals[3] is 1, so the total is 3.

q.q: What is the main advantage of a List over an array?
q.why: Lists change size with Add and Remove; arrays are fixed.

q.q: How do you find the number of items in a list called team?
q.why: Lists use Count with no brackets; arrays use Length.

q.q: Which line must be at the top of a program that uses List?
q.why: List is part of System.Collections.Generic.

q.q: Which line correctly declares an empty list of integers?
q.why: The type goes in angle brackets on both sides, followed by new and ().

q.q: names holds Aoife, Cian, Erin. After names.RemoveAt(0); what is names[0]?
q.why: RemoveAt(0) removes Aoife, and the rest move up one place.

q.q: What does towns.Contains("Omagh") give back?
q.why: Contains returns a Boolean.

q.q: In foreach (string p in team), what is p?
o: The index of each item in team
The number of items in team
The whole team list at once
Each item of team, one at a time
q.why: The loop variable holds the next item on each pass.

q.q: A program stores the rainfall for each of the 12 months of a year. Which is the better choice?
o: A list, as rainfall values are decimals
A list, as arrays cannot hold doubles
An array, as there are always 12 months
An array, as lists cannot hold numbers
q.why: The number of items is fixed and known, which suits an array.

q.q: A program adds scores to a list until -1 is typed. The user types 14, 9, 17, -1. What is the list's Count?
q.why: -1 is the stop value and is not added, so three scores are stored.

q.q: What happens if a program removes items from a list while a foreach loop is going through it?
q.why: A list cannot be changed while foreach is looping through it; C# throws an exception.

q.q: What should a running total be set to before the loop?
q.why: Starting at 0 means every item is added exactly once.

q.q: What is the average of 4, 6, 8 and 10?
q.why: The total is 28, and 28 divided by 4 is 7.

q.q: total is 417 and marks.Count is 6, both ints. What does total / marks.Count give?
q.why: Integer division throws away the .5.

q.q: Which expression correctly gives the average with its decimal part?
q.why: Cast before dividing; casting the result afterwards is too late, as the decimal is already lost.

q.q: A largest algorithm starts largest at 0. What does it report for the list -4, -2, -9?
q.why: No value is bigger than 0, so largest never changes. Start with the first item instead.

q.q: largest starts as the first item of 3, 7, 7, 5 and changes when an item is bigger. How many times does it change?
q.why: It changes from 3 to 7 once; the second 7 is equal, not bigger.

q.q: Which describes a linear search?
o: Jump straight to the middle of the list
Check each item in turn from the start
Sort the list, then check the last item
Check only the first and the last items
q.why: A linear search goes through items one after another.

q.q: In the linear search, why does position start at -1?
o: Indexes in a list start at -1
-1 can never be a real index
It makes the loop run backwards
C# requires every int to start at -1
q.why: If position is still -1 at the end, nothing was found.

q.q: A linear search for "erin" runs on a list containing "Erin". What is the result?
o: Found at index 2 of the list
Not found, as the search is case-sensitive
Found at index 0 of the list
The program crashes with an error
q.why: == compares strings exactly, including capital letters.

q.q: Using if (mark >= 50) count++; how many of 50, 49, 75, 30, 50 are counted?
q.why: 50, 75 and 50 are all at least 50.

q.q: How does a generative AI tool produce code?
o: It runs and tests every possible program first
It predicts likely code from patterns it learned
It looks the answer up in one textbook
It asks a human programmer every time
q.why: It predicts from training data; it does not run or check the code.

q.q: What is an AI hallucination?
o: Refusing to answer a question at all
Running very slowly on a busy server
Confidently giving something false or made up
q.why: Made-up methods or facts presented confidently are hallucinations.

q.q: Which is a genuine benefit of using AI when coding?
o: It always produces code with no bugs
It knows exactly what your teacher wants
It guarantees full marks in coursework
It can explain error messages in plain English
q.why: Explaining errors is a strength; the others are false claims.

q.q: Which is a real limitation of AI-generated code?
o: It can only ever be written in Python
It can look correct but still contain bugs
It is never allowed to contain comments
It is unable to use loops or IF statements
q.why: AI can be confidently wrong, so code must be checked.

q.q: Which addition to a prompt best helps a Year 10 pupil learn from the code?
o: Ask it to explain each line
Ask it to leave out comments
q.why: Explanations help you understand, check and build on the code.

q.q: AI code returns 14 as the average of 12, 15, 18 and 14 instead of 14.75. What is the most likely bug?
q.why: Dividing two ints drops the decimal: 59 / 4 gives 14.

q.q: AI code loops with for (int i = 0; i <= scores.Count; i++) and crashes. What type of bug is this?
q.why: <= runs one time too many and reads past the end of the list.

q.q: What is the best way to check that code from an AI tool works?
o: Check that it has plenty of comments and looks neat
Check that it is long enough to cover every case
Trace it, then test it with normal, boundary and erroneous data
Ask the same AI tool whether its own code is correct
q.why: Tracing and testing against expected results proves whether it works.

q.q: For GCSE coursework, what do the rules say about using AI?
o: The work must be your own and AI use acknowledged
AI can write any part as long as it compiles
AI use should be kept hidden from the teacher
AI code must be pasted in without any changes
q.why: Passing off AI work as your own is malpractice; any use must be acknowledged.

q.q: Why should you not paste classmates' names and marks into an AI chatbot?
o: Chatbots cannot read names or numbers
It would make the chatbot's answer slower
Names would turn the code into a string
It is personal data that the company may store
q.why: Other people's personal data must be protected; what you type may be kept and used.

q.q: Which order matches the software development cycle?
q.why: Plan, build, test, improve, then repeat.

q.q: A program accepts ages from 11 to 18. Which is boundary test data?
q.why: 18 is at the edge of the allowed range.

q.q: A score must be from 0 to 20. Which is erroneous test data?
q.why: 21 is just outside the range, so it should be rejected.

q.q: A score must be from 0 to 20. Which is normal test data?
q.why: 13 is a sensible value well inside the range; 0 and 20 are boundary data.

q.q: Which test table column records what should happen, worked out before the test is run?
q.why: Expected results are worked out first, then compared with the actual results.

q.q: What does int.TryParse("ten", out n) return?
q.why: TryParse returns false instead of crashing when the text is not a whole number.

q.q: What is validation?
o: Testing a program after it is finished
Checking input is allowed before it is used
Converting a string into an integer
Writing comments to explain the code
q.why: Validation rejects input that is not sensible or allowed.

q.q: After fixing one bug, why should the whole test table be run again?
o: Tests only count if they are run twice
The compiler will not run without it
A fix can create a new bug somewhere else
It makes the finished program faster
q.why: Re-testing checks that the change has not broken anything that worked before.

q.q: What is the expected average for the quiz scores 15, 8, 20 and 12?
q.why: The total is 55, and 55 divided by 4 is 13.75.

q.q: In version 1, entering -1 straight away crashed FindHighest. Why?
o: -1 cannot be stored in an int variable
scores[0] does not exist in an empty list
The list was declared as an array
q.why: With no scores, there is no first item to start from.
